source_text:
Ἀποδεχόμενός σου τὴν ἐν θεῷ γνώμην ἡδρασμένην ὡς ἐπὶ πέτραν ἀκίνητον, ὑπερδοξάζω, καταξιωθεὶς τοῦ προσώπου σου τοῦ ἀμώμου, οὗ ὀναίμην ἐν θεῷ.
παρακαλῶ σε ἐν χάριτι ᾗ ἐνδέδυσαι, προσθεῖναι τῷ δρόμῳ σου καὶ πάντας παρακαλεῖν, ἵνα σώζωνται. ἐκδίκει σου τὸν τόπον ἐν πάσῃ ἐπιμελείᾳ σαρκικῇ τε καὶ πνευματικῇ. τῆς ἑνώσεως φρόντιζε, ἧς οὐδὲν ἄμεινον, πάντας βάσταζε, ὡς καὶ σὲ ὁ κύριος: πάντων ἀνέχου ἐν ἀγάπῃ, ὥσπερ καὶ ποιεῖς.
προσευχαῖς σχόλαζε ἀδιαλείπτοις: αἰτοῦ σύνεσιν πλείονα ἧς ἔχεις: γρηγόρει ἀκοίμητον πνεῦμα κεκτημένος. τοῖς κατ’ ἄνδρα κατὰ ὁμοήθειαν θεοῦ λάλει: πάντων τὰς νόσους βάσταζε ὡς τέλειος ἀθλητής. ὅπου πλείων κόπος, πολὺ κέρδος.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna, and has just greeted him; now he begins his direct exhortation to him as a bishop.
pass_a_gloss: Approving your purpose in God [which is] fixed as on an immovable rock, I glorify [you] exceedingly, having been deemed worthy of your blameless face, of which may I have benefit in God. I urge you in the grace [with] which you have been clothed, to add to your course and to urge all, in order that they may be saved. Defend your place in all care fleshly and spiritual. Care for the unity, than which nothing [is] better; bear all, as also the Lord [bears] you; endure all in love, just as also you do. Devote yourself to prayers unceasing; ask for understanding greater than [that] which you have; be watchful, possessing a sleepless spirit. To each man according to the manner of God speak; bear the sicknesses of all as a perfect athlete. Where [there is] more labor, much gain.

choices.why: γνώμη here is Polycarp's settled intention or resolve, and 'in God' marks its divine grounding; 'purpose in God' keeps the theological frame without over-interpreting.
The compound verb intensifies δοξάζω; 'glorify exceedingly' preserves the prefix force and avoids the rare English 'over-glorify.'
δρόμος is the athletic race-course metaphor; 'add to your course' keeps the image of pressing further in the race, matching the athletic language later in the section.
τόπος is Polycarp's office or position as bishop; 'defend your place' keeps the spatial metaphor of the episcopal seat while the verb carries the sense of guarding and vindicating.
The adjective means literally 'unsleeping'; 'sleepless spirit' preserves the vivid paradox of constant vigilance as a spiritual state.

choices.english: according to the manner of God
choices.why: ὁμοήθεια is a rare word meaning likeness of character or manner; 'according to the manner of God' renders it literally while keeping the sense that Polycarp should address each person in a way that reflects God's own way.

pass_b_english: I welcome your purpose in God, fixed as on an immovable rock, and I glorify Him exceedingly, because I have been deemed worthy of your blameless face. May I have benefit from it in God.

I urge you, by the grace with which you have been clothed, to press on in your course and to urge everyone, so that they may be saved. Defend your place with all care, both fleshly and spiritual. Care for unity, than which nothing is better. Bear everyone, as the Lord also bears you. Endure everyone in love, just as you are already doing.

Devote yourself to unceasing prayers. Ask for understanding greater than what you have. Keep watch, possessing a sleepless spirit. Speak to each person according to the manner of God. Bear the illnesses of everyone as a perfect athlete. Where there is more labor, there is much gain.

last_rejected.why: νόσους here likely 'infirmities/weaknesses' metaphorically, not literal 'illnesses'; but could be valid. More critically, 'illnesses' is too narrow—'ailments' or 'infirmities' better captures metaphorical sense of others' burdens.
last_rejected.ruling: νόσους literally means 'illnesses/sicknesses'; 'infirmities' is a preference, not a major meaning change. Range is valid.

polish.changed: Clarified the first sentence by separating the greeting from the prayer for benefit, so the reader can follow Ignatius's thought without the parenthetical interruption.

notes.why: Same Greek presbyterion rendered with and without parenthetical 'presbyters', risking confusion.
notes.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note.

notes.quote: council of elders in the place of the council of the apostles
notes.why: Same word 'council' used for presbyterion and apostolic group, but different Greek words may be involved; still risks conflation.
notes.fix: Note Greek terms or use 'college of apostles' if distinct.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening sentence by naming God as the one glorified, smoothed the awkward 'add to your course' into 'press on in your course,' and kept the address direct and natural for reading aloud.

notes.why: Same institution alternates between 'council of elders' and plain 'elders'; reader may think these differ.
notes.fix: Use consistent term or gloss as 'body of elders/presbyters'.
